changes: Goviṃda: dropped 'commissioner'. 'goviṃdanāmārthaṃ' only says the copy was made for someone named Goviṃda, so the role is beneficiary. Confidence lowered to medium.
Place: as_written changed to the attested form 'bhaktāpuranivāsinā'. This phrase gives the scribe's residence; copying in Bhaktapur is only inferred from it.
Date: year field now gives the number reading. ce_approx is a tentative range. Weekday normalised to Thursday, month glossed as Phālguna. The tithi is given as a possible reading of 'harau'.
Purpose: changed to 'for Goviṃda'. 'durggā prītri astu' is a closing blessing, not a statement of purpose.

date.as_written: nepāle hāyane jāte dhaneśe nayanārṇṇave | site tapasya sutithau harauvāre vṛspatau
date.year: dhaneśe nayanārṇṇave = NS [arṇava][nayana=2][dhaneśa] (units-first chronogram); probably 72x, uncertain
date.tithi: harau = Hari's tithi, i.e. ekādaśī (or dvādaśī)?; uncertain
date.ce_approx: c. 1600–1610 (NS 72x, if arṇava=7); if arṇava=4, c. 1300–1310

notes: The catalogue names Goviṃda as the scribe, but the colophon names daivajña Viṣṇusiṃha of Bhaktapur as the scribe. He copied the text for someone named Goviṃda. Chronogram: read units first, the words give units = dhaneśa, tens = nayana (2), hundreds = arṇava. Arṇava is 4 or 7. NS 72x is more likely for a Newari manuscript of this kind. Dhaneśa (Kubera) is not a standard number word, so the units digit is uncertain; the year cannot be pinned down without checking the tithi and weekday. 'harau' may name the tithi (ekādaśī/dvādaśī) or stand for the nakṣatra Śravaṇa (ruled by Hari). 'sastaṃ' is probably for 'śastaṃ'. 'durggā prītri (!) astu' stands for 'durgā prītir astu'.
